title: Strictosamide ameliorates LPS-induced acute lung injury by targeting ERK2 and mediating NF-kappaB signaling pathway.
authors: Geng, Qi; Liu, Bin; Fan, Danping; Cao, Zhiwen; Li, Li; Lu, Peipei; Lin, Lin; Yan, Lan; Xiong, Yibai; He, Xiaojuan; Lu, Jun; Chen, Peng; Lu, Cheng
one_liner_zh: 该研究探讨天然化合物Strictosamide通过靶向ERK2调节NF-kappaB通路缓解急性肺损伤，属于小分子-蛋白互作与炎症机制研究，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Acute lung injury (ALI) ranks among the deadliest pulmonary diseases, significantly impacting mortality and morbidity. Presently, the primary treatment for ALI involves supportive therapy; however, its efficacy remains unsatisfactory. Strictosamide (STR), an indole alkaloid found in the Chinese herbal medicine Nauclea officinalis (Pierre ex Pit.) Merr. & Chun (Wutan), has been found to exhibit numerous pharmacological properties, particularly anti-inflammatory effects. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimes to systematically identify and validate the specific binding proteins targeted by STR and elucidate its anti-inflammatory mechanism in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced ALI. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Biotin chemical modification, protein microarray analysis and network pharmacology were conducted to screen for potential STR-binding proteins. The binding affinity was assessed through surface plasmon resonance (SPR), cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) and molecular docking, and the anti-inflammatory mechanism of STR in ALI treatment was assessed through in vivo and in vitro experiments. RESULTS: Biotin chemical modification, protein microarray and network pharmacology identified extracellular-signal-regulated kinase 2 (ERK2) as the most important binding proteins among 276 candidate STR-interacting proteins and nuclear factor-kappaB (NF-kappaB) pathway was one of the main inflammatory signal transduction pathways. Using SPR, CETSA, and molecular docking, we confirmed STR's affinity for ERK2. In vitro and in vivo experiments demonstrated that STR mitigated inflammation by targeting ERK2 to modulate the NF-kappaB signaling pathway in LPS-induced ALI. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings indicate that STR can inhibit the NF-kappaB signaling pathway to attenuate LPS-induced inflammation by targeting ERK2 and decreasing phosphorylation of ERK2, which could be a novel strategy for treating ALI.
abstract_zh: 民族药理学相关性：急性肺损伤（ALI）是最致命的肺部疾病之一，显著影响死亡率和发病率。目前，ALI的主要治疗手段为支持性治疗，但其疗效仍不尽如人意。蛇根碱（STR）是一种从中国草药乌檀（Nauclea officinalis (Pierre ex Pit.) Merr. & Chun，又称Wutan）中发现的吲哚生物碱，已被发现具有多种药理特性，尤其是抗炎作用。研究目的：本研究旨在系统性地识别并验证STR靶向的特异性结合蛋白，并阐明其在脂多糖（LPS）诱导的ALI中的抗炎机制。材料与方法：采用生物素化学修饰、蛋白质微阵列分析和网络药理学筛选潜在的STR结合蛋白。通过表面等离子体共振（SPR）、细胞热位移分析（CETSA）和分子对接评估结合亲和力，并通过体内和体外实验评估STR在ALI治疗中的抗炎机制。结果：生物素化学修饰、蛋白质微阵列和网络药理学鉴定出细胞外信号调节激酶2（ERK2）是276个候选STR相互作用蛋白中最重要的结合蛋白，且核因子-κB（NF-κB）通路是主要的炎症信号转导通路之一。通过SPR、CETSA和分子对接，我们确认了STR对ERK2的亲和力。体外和体内实验表明，STR通过靶向ERK2调节NF-κB信号通路，减轻LPS诱导的ALI中的炎症反应。结论：我们的研究结果表明，STR可通过靶向ERK2并降低ERK2的磷酸化来抑制NF-κB信号通路，从而减轻LPS诱导的炎症，这可能为治疗ALI提供一种新策略。
